forces.title: Declining commodity prices and elevated input costs pressure farmer profitability
forces.description: Since farmer profitability last peaked in 2021–22, commodity prices have declined while the cost of fertilizer, labor, land, equipment, and financing have remained elevated or volatile. Geopolitical tensions, such as in the Strait of Hormuz, exacerbate energy and input costs. This squeezes farm margins, leading farmers to preserve cash, delay purchases (e.g., fertilizer, farm equipment), and trade down from branded to generic inputs, creating upstream pressure on food raw material costs and availability for Food Products & Beverages.

forces.title: Farmers trading down to generic crop protection products
forces.description: Amidst high input costs and commodity price volatility, North American and European row crop farmers are increasingly shifting from branded crop protection products to generics. In Europe, 30% expect to shift to generics, compared to 7% for branded products, driven by trust in generic quality and a need for cash preservation. This trend compels agriculture input players to adapt portfolios, offering sharper value communication, flexible financing, or focusing on lower-cost products, impacting the supply chain for food products.

forces.title: Adverse weather and high input costs continue to pressure food margins
forces.description: Irish food and beverage producers face ongoing margin pressure from persistently high energy and staffing costs, global market disruption, and extreme weather impacting yields and production costs. Western Europe's exceptionally high temperatures and low rainfall in summer 2026 affect raw material availability and cost. In 2025, 91% of Irish food businesses reported increased operating costs, with 85% anticipating further increases in 2026, challenging profitability and investment in the sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Automation and operational efficiency investments rising in food production
forces.description: Food and beverage producers in Ireland are increasingly investing in automation, robotics, and integrated production methods. This strategic shift aims to improve productivity, mitigate persistent labor shortages, and manage escalating costs effectively. Businesses are also streamlining operations by insourcing previously outsourced activities and upskilling employees to support more automated environments. This reflects a structural move towards advanced manufacturing, enhancing long-term competitiveness and efficiency for food products and beverages.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: New EU packaging and deforestation regulations increase compliance burden
forces.description: Evolving EU regulations are significantly shaping food and beverage manufacturing. Regulation (EU) 2025/40 on Packaging and Packaging Waste (PPWR), effective August 2026, introduces phased recyclability, labeling, and reporting requirements, alongside bans on certain substances. From December 2026, the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) mandates companies demonstrate deforestation-free and legally produced commodities (e.g., cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, soy). Both regulations increase supply chain traceability and compliance requirements for food and beverage producers operating within or exporting to the EU.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: GLP-1 drug adoption drives significant shifts in consumer food and beverage spending
forces.description: The rapid adoption of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, with US users projected to double by 2030, is fundamentally transforming consumer behavior. Users are consuming smaller portions and less frequently, especially for salty snacks, alcohol, soft drinks, chocolate, and candy. Conversely, there's increased consumption of fresh foods, protein, fiber, and functional gut health beverages. This leads to a substantial reframe of the food and beverage portfolio towards functional and portion-right products, and rationalization in reduced categories, affecting product development and market strategy for F&B companies.
forces.source_title: The Unexpected Ways GLP-1s Are Transforming Consumer Behavior

forces.title: Growing consumer demand for high-quality, sustainable, healthier food products
forces.description: There is growing global demand for high-quality food products, driven by preferences for Mediterranean diets and sustainable production methods. This shift, coupled with an increasing consumer focus on healthier foods, creates significant opportunities for food and beverage companies, particularly those offering products aligned with these trends. This acts as a tailwind, encouraging innovation and differentiation, especially for companies like those in Greece, which are well-positioned with their quality products and export capabilities.
forces.source_title: Food and Beverages Industry. Facts & Figures 2025

forces.title: Energy market volatility and geopolitical conflicts increase agricultural input costs
forces.description: Geopolitical crises, particularly the US/Israel war with Iran affecting the Strait of Hormuz, have caused sharp increases in crude oil and natural gas prices. This directly translates to higher production costs for Irish agriculture, with transport fuel expenditure forecast to rise by 20% and electricity prices by 5% in 2026 compared to 2025. These elevated energy costs impact intensive farm systems (pigs, poultry, dairy, tillage), squeezing farm profitability and contributing to higher raw material costs for food and beverage processors.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

forces.title: Fertilizer price increases due to geopolitical conflict and energy costs
forces.description: Fertilizer prices are significantly influenced by energy costs and supply-demand dynamics. Following sharp increases in European natural gas prices due to the US/Israel attacks on Iran, fertilizer prices in 2026 are expected to be approximately 20% higher than in 2025. This rise in a core agricultural input increases production costs for dairy, beef, sheep, and tillage farms in Ireland, directly impacting the cost base for food and beverage manufacturers reliant on these raw materials.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

forces.title: Adverse weather conditions reduce Irish cereal production volume
forces.description: Unusually high rainfall from autumn 2025 to spring 2026, followed by a period of high temperatures and low rainfall in mid-July 2026, has adversely impacted Irish tillage crops. Mixed conditions during crop development stages and reduced tillage area have led to a forecast 10% decrease in total cereal production tonnage for harvest 2026 compared to 2025. This reduced domestic supply can increase reliance on imports and potentially raise raw material costs for packaged food manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

forces.title: Lower milk prices and higher costs severely impact Irish dairy margins
forces.description: Irish dairy farmers face a significant challenge in 2026 due to considerably lower milk prices and increased production costs. The average Irish milk price for 2026 is forecast to be 38 c/l (base price), down about 20% from 2025, while average total milk production costs per litre are expected to rise by 5%. This combination implies a sharp reduction in Irish dairy net margins, potentially a decrease of almost 50% compared to 2025, which could affect raw milk supply and pricing for dairy product manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

forces.title: Irish beef supply decrease leads to mixed price outlook
forces.description: EU beef supply decreased by 1.5% in Q1 2026 relative to Q1 2025 and is expected to decrease by 2.6% for the full year. While EU beef exports are slightly down, imports are expected to increase. Finished cattle prices in Ireland started 2026 at exceptional levels but declined steadily in recent months, although they remain elevated compared to 2020-2021. This mixed supply and demand dynamic creates an uncertain price environment for meat processors and consumers.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

forces.title: Mackerel fishing quota reduction impacts Irish seafood sector
forces.description: Following EU Agrifish Council negotiations in March 2026, Ireland's mackerel fishing quota was reduced by 48% (from a proposed 70%), adding approximately 8,000 tonnes to the annual national quota compared to the initial severe cut. While this provides some relief, the reduction remains substantial for Irish fishers. Higher mackerel pricing, at €5.85 per kg (+165%), is helping to offset some of the volume impact, but the overall reduction in quota still represents a significant challenge for the seafood sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: UK government proposes ban and levy changes for soft drinks
forces.description: The UK Government has confirmed a ban on highly caffeinated energy drinks for under-16s, with proposed timing likely April 2027 if passed. Additionally, a paper on the Soft Drinks Industry Levy (SDIL) proposes lowering the sugar threshold for the levy from 5g to 4.5g of added sugar per 100ml. These regulatory changes directly impact non-alcoholic beverage producers and distributors, potentially leading to reformulation efforts, changes in product offerings, and altered profitability for those operating in or exporting to the UK market.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Rise of private label products challenges national food and beverage brands
forces.description: Private label products are experiencing a new phase of growth, significantly outperforming national brands (growing roughly three times faster in 2025), even as inflation moderates. Consumers increasingly view private labels as credible alternatives in quality and innovation, not just price, with 85% believing they match or exceed national brands. Retailers are investing in tiered ranges, trend-led innovation (e.g., prebiotic soda), and expansion into new categories, creating a reinforcing cycle that challenges established food and beverage manufacturers to differentiate and innovate.
forces.source_title: The State of Grocery North America 2026

forces.title: Wellness trends reshape grocery baskets and food product demand
forces.description: Wellness is becoming more specific, functional, and behaviorally important, reshaping consumer purchasing habits in grocery. Factors like GLP-1 drug adoption, moderation trends (e.g., alcohol), and shifting health goals are changing what consumers buy. This drives demand for healthier, functional food and beverage products and alters consumption patterns for categories like snacks and alcohol. Food and beverage manufacturers must respond through assortment changes, product innovation (e.g., plant-based, organic, 'free-from'), and shelf-space shifts within retail channels.
forces.source_title: The State of Grocery North America 2026

forces.title: Growing consumer education on food provenance and local sourcing
forces.description: Consumer education on food provenance and local sourcing is growing, with initiatives such as Grow It Yourself (GIY) and Lidl Ireland's Lidl Foodies program for children raising awareness. This trend fosters demand for domestically produced food and beverages, reinforcing Ireland's strong reputation for quality, traceability, and trusted production standards. This creates opportunities for Irish food producers to highlight local origins and supply chain transparency, potentially gaining market share and premium pricing within the domestic and export markets.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Irish retail food price inflation remains elevated
forces.description: Irish grocery inflation remained elevated at approximately 4% in June/July 2026, contributing to sharp focus on food price increases for consumers. These increases are linked to global commodity prices (wheat, sugar, cocoa due to demand/supply issues), increased overheads for retailers/suppliers (personal, energy, insurance), rising farm gate prices (beef, dairy, poultry), and global trade uncertainty. This persistent inflation creates pressure on consumer spending power and challenges food and beverage producers to manage costs and pricing strategies.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish Food & Beverage sector demonstrates resilience despite H1 2026 export decline
viewpoints.description: The Irish food and beverage sector generated exports valued at €9.1bn in H1 2026, marking a modest 3% decline year-over-year. Prepared consumer foods matched 2025 exports, offsetting declines in meat, dairy, beverages, seafood, and horticulture. Despite easing food inflation in June 2026 (0.6% in Ireland, 1.7% UK, 1% EU), high input costs and weather pressures persist, suggesting elevated food prices. The sector shows resilience in managing disruption but maintains a cautious approach to H2 investment, prioritizing efficiency and competitiveness.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

viewpoints.title: Greek Food & Beverage sector maintains strong growth prospects amidst challenges
viewpoints.description: The Greek Food and Beverage industry is a resilient pillar of the Greek economy, contributing substantially to GDP and exports. It exhibits strong export momentum in EU, USA, Middle East, and Asia, benefiting from global demand for high-quality Mediterranean products and sustainable production. While facing rising energy costs, inflationary pressures, and foreign competition, the sector maintains strong growth prospects due to product quality, export dynamics, and consumer shift towards healthier foods, adapting through digital transformation and innovation.
viewpoints.source_title: Food and Beverages Industry. Facts & Figures 2025

viewpoints.title: Irish Agrifood sector stable but faces margin pressure from rising costs
viewpoints.description: Ireland’s agrifood sector in Q2 2026 remains relatively resilient, showing underlying momentum. However, profitability tightening is anticipated due to rising fuel prices and increased processing and transport costs, linked to the Middle East conflict. Smaller producers and hospitality-linked operators are particularly vulnerable. Overall, the sector is broadly stable, with near-term performance dependent on cost evolution, demand trends, and the broader macroeconomic environment, suggesting a moderate risk level.

viewpoints.title: Irish Dairy sector faces sharp income reduction due to lower prices, higher costs
viewpoints.description: The Irish dairy sector faces a challenging outlook for 2026, with average milk prices forecast to decrease by approximately 20% compared to 2025 (to 38 c/l base price). Concurrently, average total milk production costs per litre are expected to rise by about 5% to 37 cent per litre. This combination of significantly lower prices and higher costs is projected to result in a sharp reduction in Irish dairy farm net margins, potentially by almost 50% from 2025 levels, translating to an average FFI of around €78,000.
viewpoints.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish Tillage sector faces decreased output value and farm income
viewpoints.description: The Irish tillage sector is forecast to experience a decrease in market-based output value in 2026, driven by little change in cereal prices and a projected 10% reduction in production volume. Direct costs on average tillage farms are expected to increase by about 5% compared to 2025, largely due to higher fertilizer and fuel prices. Consequently, average market-based gross margins per hectare are estimated to decrease, leading to average tillage farm income remaining below €45,000.
viewpoints.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026
